Fixture: 36_icc_rgb_v4_para_32x32_lossless.jxl (+ 36_icc_rgb_v4_para_32x32_lossless.icc)
32x32 RGB, mathematically lossless, ICC v4 profile with mluc and para
tags -- the non-v2 header and type-dictionary case

Purpose
-------
Targets slice 4 (18181-1 E.4.3 and E.4.5). An ICC v4.3 profile
(version field 0x04300000) whose text tags are multiLocalizedUnicode
("mluc") and whose TRC is a parametricCurveType ("para", type 3, the sRGB
piecewise curve), with a chad matrix.

Two stages see something different from the v2 fixtures. E.4.3 predicts 4
for header byte 8 (the major version), which a v2 profile contradicts and
a v4 profile confirms -- so 31 and 36 together prove that byte is
predicted rather than copied. E.4.5's type dictionary for commands 16..23
contains "mluc" and "para" but not the v2 "desc" text layout, so a
different pair of dictionary entries is exercised.

Verification
------------
tools/make-icc-fixtures.sh checks two things on every run, and refuses to
write the fixture if either fails:

  * djxl --orig_icc_out returns a profile byte-identical to the one cjxl was
    given, so the reference really is what the codestream stores;
  * djxl decodes the pixels to a PNM byte-identical to the source, so the
    stream is mathematically lossless.

tests/e2e_icc.rs then asserts that JPXL's own E.4 decoder reproduces the
reference byte for byte, and repeats the comparison against a live djxl when
one is installed.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
